A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Stable-ChebNet research. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support comparison, including matching material across the reordered appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original ChebNet and Stable-ChebNet experiments on synthetic graph tasks, OGB datasets, and peptide benchmarks, including Tables 1–5.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds Stable-ChebNet results on four heterophilic node-classification datasets in Table 9.

M1.justification: The Chebyshev filtering, antisymmetric weight parameterization, damping term, and forward-Euler update in Section 3.3 remain unchanged. The additional benchmarks do not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: v2 adds Roman-empire, Amazon-ratings, Minesweeper, and Tolokers, extending evaluation to four standardized heterophilic node-classification settings beyond the retained synthetic, peptide, and OGB tasks. Appendix F mentions five tasks, but only these four are named and reported.

E2.justification: Table 5 adds evaluated comparisons with MP-SSM, GRAMA, and PH-DGN. New Table 9 substantially broadens the comparator set with methods such as CoGNN, NAGphormer, Polynormer, H2GCN, FAGCN, and JacobiConv, alongside retained baseline families.

E3.justification: The added heterophily evaluation specifies the cited benchmark's preprocessing and splits, accuracy for Roman-empire and Amazon-ratings, and ROC-AUC for Minesweeper and Tolokers. Existing split descriptions and the hyperparameter grids in Tables 6–8 are unchanged.

E4.justification: The supplementary K=5 eigenvalue comparison is revised: Figure 7(b) shows a changed Stable-ChebNet histogram and complex-plane point cloud. The existing ring-transfer, barbell, and polynomial-order analyses are retained; the PDFs do not explain the procedure behind the revised spectrum.

E5.justification: v2 adds a conflicting uncertainty description: checklist item 7 calls the reported uncertainties standard errors, whereas Table 1 still specifies standard deviations over four initializations, as does new Table 9. This changes the reporting documentation but does not establish a changed estimator or additional runs for existing results.

E6.justification: Table 9 adds Stable-ChebNet accuracies of 92.03 and 53.15 on Roman-empire and Amazon-ratings, and ROC-AUC scores of 95.71 and 85.55 on Minesweeper and Tolokers. Table 5 adds three comparator rows; GRAMA's 0.2436 MAE becomes the best listed peptide-struct result. Existing Tables 1–4 and shared Table 5 entries are unchanged, while Figure 7(b)'s plotted spectrum changes.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, method equations, Lemma 3.1, and Theorems 1–5 remain unchanged. The proofs formerly in Appendix C are retained in v2 Appendix B without substantive mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same claims about ChebNet's long-range capabilities, high-order instability, and stabilization through antisymmetric dynamics. The additional experiments do not redefine the central contribution.

C2.justification: Section 4 newly cautions that heterophily performance alone establishes neither long-range propagation nor resistance to oversmoothing, distinguishing these factors explicitly. The introduction also expands the heat-dissipation and preservation explanation accompanying Figure 1.

D1.justification: v2 adds a Code Availability statement naming a repository for planned public code and dataset access, plus checklist statements about accompanying reproducibility materials. The A100 hardware disclosure and hyperparameter grids are retained. The supplied PDFs do not verify repository availability or contents.

R1.justification: New Appendix A substantially expands research positioning across rewiring strategies, sparse and linear transformers, differential-equation models, ARMA and state-space approaches, and methods for measuring long-range interactions. New discussion of Arnaiz-Rodriguez and Errica also qualifies the relationship between heterophily and long-range evaluation.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose is retained, with localized explanatory additions and the new heterophily discussion. v2 reorders appendices, converts the baseline paragraph into a categorized list, adds related-work, code-availability, funding, and checklist sections, and makes small title and affiliation edits.

P2.justification: v2 adds the substantial heterophily comparison table, expands and relocates Table 5, and groups the hyperparameter tables together. Figure 1 gains explanatory annotations, Figure 6 replaces the numerical barbell illustration with a colored schematic, and Figure 7(b) changes its plots and histogram scale. These extend beyond numerical table updates or pagination.

improvement.justification: The added heterophily evaluation and peptide comparators better establish applicability and competitive context, while Section 4 usefully limits what heterophily scores imply. Expanded related work and code-access information also help readers. These gains are tempered by the new standard-error versus standard-deviation inconsistency; the core method, proofs, and retained benchmark results remain unchanged.
